title: Complete C# Developer Roadmap
description: From the type system to async and memory management — everything a C# interview covers.

modules.title: Language Foundations
modules.description: Types, memory model and object orientation.

lessons.title: Value types and reference types
lessons.content:
## Value vs reference semantics
- **Value types** (`struct`, `enum`, numeric types, `DateTime`) store data directly and are **copied** on assignment.
- **Reference types** (`class`, `string`, arrays, delegates) store a reference to a heap object; assignment copies the reference.

## Strings are special
`string` is a reference type with **value equality** and **immutability**: every modification creates a new string.

## Interview tips
- Explain *boxing*: converting a value type to `object` allocates on the heap.
- Know when to choose a `struct`: small (≤ 16 bytes), immutable, value-like (e.g. `Point`, `Money`).

lessons.title: Classes, inheritance and polymorphism
lessons.content:
## Four pillars in C#
- **Encapsulation** — access modifiers and properties protect invariants.
- **Inheritance** — single class inheritance, many interfaces.
- **Polymorphism** — `virtual`/`override` dispatches at runtime; `new` only hides.
- **Abstraction** — abstract classes and interfaces.

## Interfaces vs abstract classes
Interfaces describe capabilities and can have default implementations (C# 8+) but no instance state. Abstract classes share state and code among related types.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: C# fundamentals quiz
lessons.content: Test yourself on the fundamentals before moving on.

modules.title: Collections, Generics and LINQ
modules.description: Choosing collections and writing efficient queries.

lessons.title: Choosing the right collection
lessons.content:
| Need | Collection | Complexity |
|---|---|---|
| Ordered list, index access | `List<T>` | O(1) index, O(1)* append |
| Key → value lookup | `Dictionary<K,V>` | O(1) average |
| Uniqueness | `HashSet<T>` | O(1) average |
| Sorted keys | `SortedDictionary<K,V>` | O(log n) |
| FIFO / LIFO | `Queue<T>` / `Stack<T>` | O(1) |
| Priority | `PriorityQueue<T,P>` | O(log n) |

Generics avoid boxing and give compile-time type safety. Variance (`out T`) is only on interfaces and delegates.

lessons.title: LINQ and deferred execution
lessons.content:
LINQ operators like `Where` and `Select` are **deferred**: they run when enumerated. Operators like `Count()`, `ToList()` and `First()` execute immediately.

- Materialise once with `ToList()` if you enumerate multiple times.
- `IQueryable<T>` sends expression trees to a provider (EF Core → SQL); `IEnumerable<T>` runs in memory.
- `Single()` asserts exactly one element; `First()` takes the first.

lessons.title: Exercise: refactor loops to LINQ
lessons.content: Practise expressing loops declaratively.
lessons.exercise: Given a list of orders (Id, CustomerId, Total, CreatedAt), write LINQ queries that: (1) return the top 3 customers by total spend, (2) group orders by month with totals, (3) find customers with no orders in the last 30 days. Then explain which queries would be translated to SQL by EF Core and which would run in memory.

modules.title: Async, Errors and Memory
modules.description: Production-grade async code and resource management.

lessons.title: How async/await really works
lessons.content:
`await` on an incomplete task **returns to the caller** and resumes later as a continuation. No thread is blocked while I/O is in flight.

**Rules**
1. Async all the way — never `.Result`/`.Wait()` (deadlocks, thread-pool starvation).
2. Run independent I/O concurrently with `Task.WhenAll`.
3. `async void` only for event handlers.
4. Pass `CancellationToken` through every async call.
5. Use `SemaphoreSlim` instead of `lock` around `await`.

lessons.title: Garbage collection and IDisposable
lessons.content:
The GC is generational (Gen0/1/2) plus the **Large Object Heap** for objects ≥ 85,000 bytes. It reclaims managed memory only.

`IDisposable` releases **unmanaged** resources deterministically — use `using` / `await using`. The GC never calls `Dispose`; it may run finalizers.

Reduce allocations in hot paths with `Span<T>`, `ArrayPool<T>` and `StringBuilder`.

lessons.title: Exceptions done right
lessons.content:
- Rethrow with `throw;` to keep the stack trace.
- Catch specific exceptions; don't use exceptions for control flow.
- `finally` always runs when leaving `try` (except process termination).
- Wrap low-level exceptions with context using `InnerException`.

title: ASP.NET Core Developer Roadmap
description: Build, secure and scale production Web APIs with ASP.NET Core.

modules.title: Hosting, Pipeline and DI
modules.description: How a request flows through an ASP.NET Core app.

lessons.title: The request pipeline
lessons.content:
Middleware runs **in registration order** on the way in and in **reverse** on the way out. Typical order:

1. Exception handling
2. HTTPS redirection / HSTS
3. Static files
4. Routing
5. CORS
6. Authentication → Authorization
7. Endpoints

`app.Run` is terminal; `app.Use` can call `next`.

lessons.title: Dependency injection lifetimes
lessons.content:
- **Transient** — new instance per resolution.
- **Scoped** — one per request (DbContext).
- **Singleton** — one per application; must be thread-safe.

Avoid **captive dependencies** (singleton → scoped). In background services create scopes with `IServiceScopeFactory`.

lessons.title: Configuration and options
lessons.content:
Providers override in order: appsettings.json → appsettings.{Env}.json → user secrets → environment variables → command line.

Bind sections to typed classes with `services.Configure<T>(config.GetSection("X"))` and inject `IOptions<T>`. Keep secrets in environment variables or a vault — never in source control.

modules.title: Building Web APIs
modules.description: Controllers, minimal APIs, filters and HTTP semantics.

lessons.title: HTTP semantics for APIs
lessons.content:
- `201 Created` + Location for new resources; `204 No Content` for empty success.
- `400` validation, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not found, `409` conflict, `429` rate limited.
- PUT/DELETE are idempotent; make POST retries safe with idempotency keys.
- Version your API (`/api/v1`) and return a consistent error envelope.

lessons.title: Controllers, minimal APIs and filters
lessons.content:
`[ApiController]` enables automatic 400 responses and binding inference. Minimal APIs (`MapGet`, `MapGroup`) are lighter for simple endpoints.

Filters run inside MVC: authorization → resource → action → result, with exception filters for MVC errors. Prefer **middleware** for global exception handling.

lessons.title: Exercise: design an orders API
lessons.content: Design endpoints for an orders service.
lessons.exercise: Design REST endpoints for creating, listing (with filtering, sorting and cursor pagination), updating and cancelling orders. Specify routes, methods, status codes, request/response DTOs, validation rules and how you would make 'create order' safe to retry.

modules.title: Security and Performance
modules.description: Authentication, authorization and scaling an API.

lessons.title: JWT authentication and refresh tokens
lessons.content:
Access tokens should be **short-lived** (minutes) because self-contained JWTs can't be revoked easily. Pair them with **refresh tokens** stored hashed on the server, **rotated** on every use, with reuse detection that revokes the family.

Validate signature, issuer, audience and lifetime. Use policies (`RequireRole`, `RequireClaim`) for authorization.

lessons.title: Performance and resilience
lessons.content:
- Use `IHttpClientFactory` with timeouts, retries (exponential backoff + jitter) and circuit breakers.
- Avoid sync-over-async to prevent thread-pool starvation.
- Cache judiciously (in-memory, distributed, output caching).
- Add rate limiting and health checks; observe with OpenTelemetry traces and metrics.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: ASP.NET Core quiz
lessons.content: Verify your understanding of ASP.NET Core.

title: Full Stack .NET Developer Roadmap
description: Connect C#, ASP.NET Core, EF Core, SQL Server and React into one coherent skill set.

modules.title: Data Access with EF Core and SQL
modules.description: From LINQ to efficient SQL.

lessons.title: EF Core essentials
lessons.content:
- `DbContext` is scoped and not thread-safe; it implements **Unit of Work**.
- Use migrations for schema changes; generate idempotent scripts for production.
- Prefer projections (`Select` into DTOs) and `AsNoTracking()` for reads.
- Watch for **N+1** queries — use `Include` or projections.

lessons.title: Indexes every developer should know
lessons.content: A **clustered index** orders the table; **nonclustered** indexes point back to it. Make predicates **SARGable**, add **INCLUDE** columns to cover queries, and read execution plans for Key Lookups and scans.

modules.title: Frontend with React
modules.description: Modern React for .NET developers.

lessons.title: Components, state and effects
lessons.content: Components are functions of props and state. Updates are batched; use functional updates when the next state depends on the previous. Effects synchronise with external systems and need honest dependency arrays.

lessons.title: Calling your API from React
lessons.content:
- Centralise API calls with typed clients.
- Handle loading, error and empty states explicitly.
- Store access tokens in memory; refresh with HttpOnly cookies or a refresh endpoint.
- Cancel requests on unmount with `AbortController`.

modules.title: Putting it together
modules.description: Architecture and delivery.

lessons.title: Clean architecture for full-stack apps
lessons.content: Keep business rules in Domain/Application layers, implement persistence and integrations in Infrastructure, and expose DTOs from the API. Dependencies point inward, which keeps logic testable.

lessons.title: Exercise: end-to-end feature
lessons.content: Implement a feature across all layers.
lessons.exercise: Implement 'bookmark a question': a SQL table with a unique (UserId, QuestionId) index, an EF Core configuration, an application service with validation, POST/DELETE endpoints returning proper status codes, and a React button with optimistic UI that rolls back on failure.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: full-stack assessment
lessons.content: A timed assessment across the stack.

title: React Developer Roadmap
description: Components, hooks, state management, routing and performance.

modules.title: React Fundamentals
modules.description: Thinking in components.

lessons.title: JSX, props and state
lessons.content:
- Props flow **down** and are read-only.
- State is local; lift it to the nearest common ancestor when shared.
- Lists need stable `key`s for reconciliation.
- Controlled inputs keep form values in state.

lessons.title: How rendering works
lessons.content: State change → render (pure) → reconciliation (diff by type and key) → commit (DOM updates) → effects. Rendering may be interrupted in concurrent mode; commits are synchronous.

modules.title: Hooks in Depth
modules.description: useState, useEffect, useRef, useMemo and custom hooks.

lessons.title: The rules and the classic pitfalls
lessons.content:
1. Call hooks at the top level only.
2. Effects capture the render's props/state — beware **stale closures**.
3. `useRef` stores mutable values without re-rendering.
4. `useMemo` caches values; `useCallback` caches function identity.

lessons.title: Exercise: build a useDebounce hook
lessons.content: Write a reusable custom hook.
lessons.exercise: Implement `useDebounce(value, delayMs)` that returns the value only after it stops changing for delayMs. Use it in a search box that fetches results with AbortController so outdated requests are cancelled. Write a test with fake timers.

modules.title: State, Routing and Performance
modules.description: Scaling React apps.

lessons.title: State management options
lessons.content: Local state → lifted state → context (low-frequency global data) → stores like Redux Toolkit or Zustand for complex, high-frequency state. Reducers must be pure; RTK uses Immer for safe 'mutations'.

lessons.title: Routing and performance
lessons.content: Use `<Link>` for client-side navigation and `useParams` for route data. For performance: measure with the Profiler, memoise selectively with `React.memo`, virtualise long lists and split code with `lazy`.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: React quiz
lessons.content: Review React fundamentals.

title: SQL Server Developer Roadmap
description: Write correct, fast T-SQL and design solid schemas.

modules.title: Querying
modules.description: Joins, subqueries and CTEs.

lessons.title: Joins without surprises
lessons.content:
- INNER returns matches only; LEFT keeps all left rows.
- Filtering the right table in WHERE turns a LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN — put such predicates in ON.
- CROSS JOIN = Cartesian product.

lessons.title: Subqueries, NULLs and CTEs
lessons.content: `NOT IN` with a NULL in the list returns no rows — use `NOT EXISTS`. CTEs improve readability and enable recursion but are not materialised.

modules.title: Analytics with Window Functions
modules.description: Ranking, running totals and top-N per group.

lessons.title: Window functions
lessons.content: `ROW_NUMBER`, `RANK`, `DENSE_RANK`, `LAG/LEAD` and aggregates with `OVER (PARTITION BY … ORDER BY … ROWS …)`. They are evaluated after WHERE, so filter on them in an outer query or CTE.

lessons.title: Exercise: top earners per department
lessons.content: Solve a classic interview problem with SQL.
lessons.exercise: Solve the 'Top Earner per Department' and 'Second Highest Salary' SQL coding challenges. Then rewrite each with a different approach (window function vs. aggregate/subquery) and compare their execution plans.

modules.title: Performance and Transactions
modules.description: Indexes, plans, isolation and locking.

lessons.title: Indexes and execution plans
lessons.content: Read actual plans; look for scans on large tables, Key Lookups, spills and estimate errors. Make predicates SARGable and add covering indexes. Beware parameter sniffing.

lessons.title: Transactions and isolation
lessons.content: READ COMMITTED (default) prevents dirty reads; REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE prevent more anomalies with more locking. RCSI/SNAPSHOT use row versions so readers don't block writers. Handle deadlock victims (error 1205) with retries.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: SQL Server quiz
lessons.content: Validate your SQL Server knowledge.

title: JavaScript Developer Roadmap
description: The language, the event loop and the browser.

modules.title: Core Language
modules.description: Types, scope and functions.

lessons.title: Types and equality
lessons.content: Primitive types vs objects, `typeof null === 'object'`, floating-point precision, and why to prefer `===`. `const` prevents reassignment, not mutation.

lessons.title: Scope, hoisting and closures
lessons.content: `var` is function-scoped; `let`/`const` are block-scoped with a TDZ. Closures capture variables, not values — the classic `var` loop prints 3 3 3.

modules.title: Asynchronous JavaScript
modules.description: Promises, async/await and the event loop.

lessons.title: The event loop
lessons.content: Synchronous code → microtasks (promises) → render → next macrotask (timers, events). Long tasks block the UI.

lessons.title: Promises and async/await
lessons.content: `async` functions return promises. Use `Promise.all` for fail-fast concurrency, `allSettled` when partial failure is fine, and `try/catch` with `await` for errors.

modules.title: Objects and the Browser
modules.description: Prototypes, this and DOM performance.

lessons.title: Prototypes and this
lessons.content: Property lookup walks the prototype chain. `this` depends on the call site, except in arrow functions, which capture it lexically.

lessons.title: Browser internals
lessons.content: Event delegation, reflow vs repaint, and storage choices (cookies vs Web Storage). Animate `transform` and `opacity`, debounce input handlers.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: JavaScript quiz
lessons.content: Test your JavaScript knowledge.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: The patterns behind most coding interview problems.

modules.title: Complexity and Arrays
modules.description: Big-O and array techniques.

lessons.title: Big-O analysis
lessons.content: Count dominant operations, drop constants. Know common classes: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²), O(2ⁿ). Amortised analysis explains O(1) appends.

lessons.title: Two pointers and sliding windows
lessons.content: Sorted arrays → two pointers from both ends. Contiguous subarrays → sliding window or Kadane's algorithm. These turn O(n²) brute force into O(n).

lessons.title: Practice: arrays and strings
lessons.content: Solve challenges to apply the techniques.
lessons.exercise: Solve 'Two Sum', 'Reverse Words', 'Valid Palindrome' and 'Sliding Window Maximum' in the coding section. For each, state the brute-force complexity and your optimised complexity.

modules.title: Linked Structures and Trees
modules.description: Lists, stacks, queues, trees and heaps.

lessons.title: Linked lists, stacks and queues
lessons.content: Pointer manipulation (reverse, merge, cycle detection), stacks for matching/undo, queues for BFS. Know their complexities and trade-offs versus arrays.

lessons.title: Trees and heaps
lessons.content: BST in-order traversal is sorted; balance matters (O(log n) vs O(n)). Heaps give O(1) min and O(log n) updates — the basis of priority queues and top-K problems.

modules.title: Graphs, Sorting and DP
modules.description: Advanced patterns.

lessons.title: Graph algorithms
lessons.content: BFS (unweighted shortest path), DFS (connectivity, cycle detection), topological sort (DAGs), Dijkstra (non-negative weights).

lessons.title: Sorting and dynamic programming
lessons.content: Merge sort is stable O(n log n); quicksort is fast on average but O(n²) worst case. DP needs overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure; choose memoisation or tabulation.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: DSA quiz
lessons.content: Check your algorithmic knowledge.

title: System Design
description: Scalability, caching, data and reliability for system design interviews.

modules.title: Foundations
modules.description: A framework for any design question.

lessons.title: How to approach a design interview
lessons.content:
1. Clarify requirements (functional + non-functional).
2. Estimate scale (QPS, storage, bandwidth).
3. Define APIs and the data model.
4. Draw a high-level design.
5. Deep-dive bottlenecks: caching, sharding, queues.
6. Discuss trade-offs, failure modes and monitoring.

lessons.title: Caching strategies
lessons.content: Cache-aside, read-through, write-through, write-behind; TTLs and invalidation; stampede protection with request coalescing and jitter.

modules.title: Data at Scale
modules.description: Replication, partitioning and consistency.

lessons.title: Replication and consistency
lessons.content: Read replicas scale reads but introduce lag. CAP: choose consistency or availability during partitions. Provide read-your-writes where users expect it.

lessons.title: Partitioning
lessons.content: Shard by a well-distributed key; avoid monotonic keys that create hotspots. Consistent hashing minimises data movement when nodes change.

modules.title: Reliability and Practice
modules.description: Async processing, resilience and a full design.

lessons.title: Queues and resilience
lessons.content: Queues decouple producers and consumers; at-least-once delivery requires idempotent consumers. Protect dependencies with timeouts, retries with jitter, circuit breakers and rate limiting.

lessons.title: Practice: design a URL shortener
lessons.content: Apply the framework end to end.
lessons.exercise: Design a URL shortener for 100M links/month. Produce estimates, API definitions, ID generation strategy, storage choice, caching, analytics pipeline and failure handling. Then compare your design with the reference answer and run it as an AI mock interview.

title: Senior Software Engineer Preparation
description: Design principles, architecture and leadership topics for senior interviews.

modules.title: Design Principles
modules.description: SOLID and patterns that senior engineers apply daily.

lessons.title: SOLID with real examples
lessons.content: SRP: one reason to change. OCP: extend via new implementations. LSP: subtypes keep the base contract. ISP: small role interfaces. DIP: depend on abstractions owned by the policy layer.

lessons.title: Patterns that matter
lessons.content: Strategy, Decorator, Factory, Observer — know when *not* to use a pattern. Prefer composition; keep abstractions earning their keep.

modules.title: Architecture
modules.description: Monoliths, microservices and boundaries.

lessons.title: Architectural styles
lessons.content: Clean/hexagonal architecture, modular monoliths, microservices with database-per-service, sagas and the outbox pattern. Choose based on team size, domain stability and operational maturity.

lessons.title: Exercise: architecture decision record
lessons.content: Practise communicating trade-offs.
lessons.exercise: Write an Architecture Decision Record (context, decision, alternatives, consequences) for splitting a notification feature out of a monolith. Include data ownership, failure handling, deployment and how you would measure success.

modules.title: Leading Technically
modules.description: Quality, delivery and behavioural interviews.

lessons.title: Code review, testing and delivery
lessons.content: Review for correctness, readability and risk; test business rules at the unit level and integrations at the boundaries; deliver safely with feature flags, blue-green or canary releases and backward-compatible migrations.

lessons.title: Behavioural stories with STAR
lessons.content: Prepare 6–8 stories using **Situation, Task, Action, Result**: conflict, failure, influence without authority, mentoring, a hard technical decision and a delivery under pressure. Quantify results and reflect on what you'd change.

title: Android Developer Preparation
description: Kotlin, coroutines and the Android architecture questions interviewers ask.

modules.title: Kotlin Essentials
modules.description: Language features used every day on Android.

lessons.title: Null safety and data classes
lessons.content: Kotlin distinguishes nullable (`String?`) and non-null types. Use `?.`, `?:` and avoid `!!`. Data classes generate equals/hashCode/copy — ideal for immutable UI state.

lessons.title: Coroutines and Flow
lessons.content: `suspend` functions suspend without blocking threads. Use structured concurrency (`viewModelScope`), switch to `Dispatchers.IO` for blocking work, and expose state with `StateFlow`. Cancel work tied to lifecycles.

modules.title: App Architecture
modules.description: MVVM, unidirectional data flow and offline-first.

lessons.title: MVVM with Jetpack Compose
lessons.content: ViewModels expose immutable `UiState` via `StateFlow`; composables render state and send events up. Repositories combine network and Room caches. Hilt provides dependencies.

lessons.title: Offline-first data
lessons.content: Treat the local database as the source of truth, sync in the background with WorkManager, resolve conflicts deterministically (e.g. last-writer-wins with timestamps), and show sync status to users.

lessons.title: Exercise: design an offline notes feature
lessons.content: Apply MVVM and offline sync.
lessons.exercise: Design a notes feature that works offline: Room entities with a pending-sync flag, a repository that writes locally then enqueues a WorkManager sync, a conflict rule, and a Compose screen showing sync state. Describe the tests you would write.
